feature: Arrow keys step by the grid
summary: With the grid on and Snap to grid on, an arrow key now moves a layer to the next grid line instead of one point, so the keyboard and a drag put things in the same places. Hold Command for the old one point press.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next. Show grid is off until you switch it on in the Canvas section of the panel; Snap to grid is on by default.

try.do: Draw a rectangle anywhere, with the grid still off.
Click bare canvas, then tick Show grid in the Canvas section of the panel.
Click the rectangle and press the right arrow once.
Press the right arrow twice more, and watch the box walk line to line.
Press Shift and the right arrow: it travels two cells, still landing on a line.
Hold Command and press the right arrow: one point, off the grid, the same way Command frees a drag.
Shift-click a second shape and press an arrow: the pair travels together and the block lands on a line.
Zoom in to 400% and press an arrow again: the step gets finer with the lines, four points instead of thirty two.

evaluate: The first press on an off-grid box moves it a part cell to rejoin the grid. Does that read as helpful or as the box jumping?
At 100% a four point grid draws 32 point lines, so one press travels 32 points. Is that the distance you expected from an arrow key?
Shift travels two cells at that spacing. Too little for a big nudge, about right, or too much?
Is Command the escape hatch you would reach for when you want one point?
Does the line under Snap to grid tell you the keys changed before you find out by pressing one?
rough: The step follows the ZOOM, because it follows the lines actually drawn: 32 points at 100% on a four point grid, four points at 400%. That is deliberate, so the keys and a drag agree, but it does mean the same key covers different ground at different zooms.
Shift is the same ten points it always covered, rounded up to whole cells, never fewer than two. On a one point grid it is still exactly ten. Nothing in the app says that number out loud yet.

The X and Y fields in the panel still step by one point per press. They have no zoom of their own and a typed number is not a drag, so they were left alone. Say the word if they should follow the grid too.
A grid set to Columns only pulls sideways, so up and down stay at one point. Correct, but there is no hint on screen that the two axes now behave differently.
Verified in the probe app with a scripted walk, Screen Recording granted, so the pictures here are real captures rather than offscreen renders.
